abstract_results: Intervals ignoring relatedness over-covered close relatives and under-covered distant candidates; for held-out clusters, split-conformal and cross-validation-plus intervals covered {scp_R2_cov} and {cvp_R2_cov} of phenotypes at nominal 0.90, and the classical Gaussian interval {pev_R2_cov}. Kinship-aware intervals covered {kincp_R2_cov}, with relatedness-conditional coverage error {kincp_R2_cond} against {cvp_R2_cond} for cross-validation-plus and {pev_R2_cond} for the Gaussian interval, and the smallest or joint-smallest error for all three predictors. The gains were in calibration, not in interval score. Ablation showed that the calibration pool spanning distant relatives was decisive: a parametric calibration fitted to the same pool performed equally well.
abstract_conclusion: Prediction intervals for selection candidates should be calibrated along the relatedness axis, at the cost of about ten additional model fits.
article_summary: Breeders need honest uncertainty for genomic predictions of individual selection candidates. We show that standard distribution-free prediction intervals become unreliable for candidates that are weakly related to the training population, because they are calibrated on close relatives. Using the classical prediction error variance as a measure of relatedness, we propose a kinship-aware calibration that draws calibration residuals from both close and distant relatives. Across ten plant and animal species, three prediction models and a simulation, it restored near-nominal coverage across relatedness levels, whereas standard intervals covered as little as {cvp_R2_cov} of phenotypes on average for new genomic clusters.
cover_finding_1: Relatedness-blind conformal intervals (split conformal, CV+) over-cover close relatives and under-cover distant candidates. For candidates from held-out genomic clusters their mean coverage of nominal 90% intervals fell to {scp_R2_cov}–{cvp_R2_cov}.
cover_finding_2: KinCP achieved the lowest, or joint-lowest, relatedness-conditional coverage error in all deployment regimes and for all three predictors (GBLUP, RKHS, LightGBM). The classical PEV-based Gaussian interval lost calibration under cluster-out deployment (mean coverage {pev_R2_cov}; KinCP {kincp_R2_cov}).
cover_finding_3: Ablations show that the relatedness-diverse calibration pool, rather than conformalisation itself, is the decisive ingredient. We report this openly and give practical recommendations.
sim_paragraph: **Simulation with known genetic values** (Table 6; Figure 7). In simulations with known additive genetic values on real loblolly pine, pig and maize genotypes ({sim_n_runs} analyses), KinCP covered {sim_kincp_R1_cov} under R1 and {sim_kincp_R2_cov} under R2. CV+ covered {sim_cvp_R1_cov} and {sim_cvp_R2_cov}, SCP {sim_scp_R2_cov} under R2, and Gauss-PEV {sim_pev_R2_cov} under R2. Mean worst-quintile coverage under R2 was {sim_kincp_R2_worst} for KinCP and {sim_pev_R2_worst} for Gauss-PEV. Because the simulated traits satisfy the Gaussian additive model exactly, Gauss-PEV is the correctly specified reference here. KinCP approached it without using the model's distributional assumptions, whereas relatedness-blind conformal intervals under-covered under R2. The relatedness covariate itself was calibrated for the genetic values. By quintile of *d*, the realised mean squared error of the genetic-value prediction divided by σ̂²_g·*d* ranged from {pevcal_R1_min} to {pevcal_R1_max} under R1 and from {pevcal_R2_min} to {pevcal_R2_max} under R2 (median over analyses; 1 = perfect calibration).
explore_paragraph: **Exploratory refinements (not pre-specified).** Two attempts to close the remaining gap under R2 did not improve on KinCP. Inner cluster folds matched to the deployment clusters (KinCP-G) gave a conditional error of {ex_kincpg_R2_cond}, against {ex_kincp_R2_cond} for KinCP on the same runs. Group-conditional (Mondrian) quantiles within quintiles of *d* gave {ex_mondrian_R2_cond}. The residual under-coverage of the least-related candidates is therefore not explained by the granularity of the inner cluster folds. We report this negative result for completeness.
granularity_paragraph: **Granularity of the deployment clusters.** The cluster-out conclusions did not depend on the number of deployment clusters, even though KinCP's inner cluster folds were kept at the pre-specified *k* = 5. With *k* = 3 larger, more distinct held-out groups, mean coverage was {gr_kincp_R2k3_cov} for KinCP, {gr_cvp_R2k3_cov} for CV+, {gr_scp_R2k3_cov} for SCP and {gr_pev_R2k3_cov} for Gauss-PEV. With *k* = 10 smaller groups, it was {gr_kincp_R2k10_cov}, {gr_cvp_R2k10_cov}, {gr_scp_R2k10_cov} and {gr_pev_R2k10_cov}. KinCP had a lower conditional error than CV+ in {gr_st_cvp_R2k3_wins} units (*k* = 3; unadjusted Wilcoxon *P* {gr_st_cvp_R2k3_p}) and {gr_st_cvp_R2k10_wins} units (*k* = 10; *P* {gr_st_cvp_R2k10_p}). Holding out each of the four real F2 families of eastern oyster in turn gave coverage of {gr_kincp_R2fam_cov} for KinCP, {gr_pev_R2fam_cov} for Gauss-PEV, {gr_cvp_R2fam_cov} for CV+ and {gr_scp_R2fam_cov} for SCP.
